name: VentureTech Alliance
identity_check: Confirmed as VentureTech Alliance (vtalliance.com), the San Jose, California venture investment management company that its site says was founded in 2001 to invest in early-stage semiconductor and other emerging-technology companies and 'currently manages funds totaling $165 million'. Backers, only as pages state them: the firm's site says it 'has a strong strategic partnership with TSMC, the IC foundry industry leader' while its investment activity 'is managed independently of this strategic partnership'; TechNode (June 2023, citing Icsmart) calls it 'TSMC's venture capital arm' and says TSMC founded it in 2001; Eliyan's 2024 release calls it the 'venture arm of world's leading foundry'; Tech Times (2026) says 'the fund has ties to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company'. TSMC's own annual reports list VentureTech Alliance Fund II, L.P. and Fund III, L.P. (Cayman Islands) as TSMC subsidiaries with 98% shareholding, and its 2024 report says both were dissolved in 2025. Archived team bios tie the staff to TSMC (Ron Norris, ex-President of TSMC USA; Christy Chou, ex-Finance Manager of TSMC North America). Company releases from 2023-2026 name Kai Tsang as its Managing Director / Managing Partner, matching the archived team page. Not TSMC's other venture vehicles listed separately in the same filings (InveStar funds, Emerging Fund, L.P.). The lead's 'deep tech / hardware, Series A' tags are broader than the site's semiconductor-value-chain focus.

open_items: Fund sizes and close dates are not published. TSMC's 2023 annual report gives incorporation dates and year-end capital (Fund II US$3,487k; Fund III US$93,998k; TSMC invested US$3,417,545 and US$92,118,263, 98% each), which are paid-in balances, not commitments. The site's 'funds totaling $165 million' figure is undated. TSMC's 2024 report says both funds were dissolved in 2025; the vehicle behind the 2025-2026 deals is not named on any fetched page.

A first fund is not named. TSMC's 2013 report lists Emerging Alliance Fund, L.P. (Jan. 10, 2001, 99.5% TSMC) and VentureTech Alliance Holdings, LLC (Apr. 25, 2007, 100%) among TSMC subsidiaries; no page ties Emerging Alliance Fund to VentureTech Alliance, so it is not recorded as Fund I. TSMC's Emerging Fund, L.P. (2021) is a separate TSMC vehicle with no stated VTA link.

Rounds seen but not recorded because the page does not place VentureTech Alliance in that round: Ayar Labs Series D, Dec 2024 (VTA listed only among 'existing investors'); Ayar Labs Series E (Mar 2026) and $150M expansion (Sep 2026) (VTA only in boilerplate); EnCharge AI Series B, Feb 2025 (VTA called a 'previous investor', not listed as a Series B participant); Ethernovia Series B, Jan 2026 (VTA not named; TechNode's 2023 '$64 million' Ethernovia figure has no round page).

Unverified database hints not checked: an Eridu investment dated 20 Mar 2026 (PitchBook snippet; eridu.ai returned 403); Tracxn lists Astera Labs and Rivos among exits. Business Wire originals for Enfabrica (Nov 2024) and Celestial AI (Aug 2025) returned 403, so a reprint and press were used.
No round found in which VentureTech Alliance led; leads=false follows the site's statement that it usually invests alongside other leads.

The live team (02team.php), portfolio (03portfolio.php) and contact (04contact.php) pages return empty documents (Oct 2026), and Wayback snapshots since 2023-06 are empty or bot-check pages. Partners and portfolio come from 2022-2023 snapshots, so current staffing is unconfirmed; titles are not given in the page text.
Stages: the firm says 'early to mid-stage'; mapping that to Series A and Series B is an interpretation, not the firm's words.
